text:
max: Heads-up: we had a weird cascade this morning in eu-central-1 where several dedicated slices were forced into cross-region fallback (-> eu-west-1) and cost spiked. Root cause looks like NIC firmware 2.7.1 flow-steer regression on rack-33.

tasha: saw the alert. grafana snapshot: https://grafana/redwood/d/egress?var-host=rack-33&from=now-1h

eric: what happened to local routing? why did scheduler move traffic across region?

max: allocator flagged host as degraded due to high tx retry rates and our smart-routing policy preferred fallback to a compatible cluster in eu-west rather than queued retries. That caused 1500 requests to cross-region in 10m.

nina: ouch. can you paste ethtool/qdisc and a small pcap? also any dmesg flow-steer warnings?

max: quick ethtool -S snippet:
```
eth0: tx_errors 0 tx_dropped 0
eth1: tx_errors 182 tx_dropped 46
eth1_flow_steer_warn: 47
```

max: dmesg shows repeated "flow_steer: miss for hash" warnings and NIC firmware logs show a retry storm.

oliver: infra-bot: created incident INFRA-7002 and set P2. Notified oncall. :rotating_light:

infra-bot: [AUDIT] incident INFRA-7002 opened by max (reason: NIC firmware regression causing cross-region fallback).

tasha: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily set routing policy to prefer local fallback (queue) for eu-central slices to avoid cross-region fallback for 30m, 2) steer the most latency-sensitive tenants off rack-33 to spare-dedicated-euc, 3) collect pcaps and run firmware rollback test in bench. Anyone object?

eric: prefer (2) + (3). (1) is fine but might delay recoveries; we risk local SLO blips vs cost. I'd rather isolate noisy host.

nina: commands I'll run now to move tenants and capture trace:
```
./bin/routectl isolate-host --host rack-33 --reason "firmware flow-steer regression" --ttl 1800
./bin/routectl steer --tenant Q --to spare-dedicated-euc --ttl 1800
tcpdump -w /tmp/rack-33-fallback.pcap -i eth1 -s 0 -c 40000
journalctl -k | egrep "flow_steer|firmware" > /tmp/rack33_fwlog.txt
```

max: running isolate-host now. infra-bot: audit entry. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: [AUDIT] isolate-host invoked by nina for rack-33 TTL=1800

oliver: finance-bot ping: we just exceeded the cross-region data transfer threshold for the month by 2.3GB with that event; auto-notify. @finance-bot can you post the immediate delta?

finance-bot: [ALERT] estimated incremental egress cost due to fallback event ~+$14.5 for the 10m window. Notified billing owners.

tasha: thanks. short-term cost is small but if this repeats nightly it's bigger. Nina, after steer can you run a quick firmware rollback test on one bench NIC and confirm behavior?

nina: yes. bench plan: rollback NIC fw 2.7.1 -> 2.7.0 and run a synthetic burst test to see if flow-steer warnings return. Will log results to INFRA-7002.

eric: ops follow-up: propose adding a scheduler weight that avoids placing VF-heavy slices on hosts with fw version >=2.7.1 until vendor confirms. Also add a config toggle in smart-routing: prefer local queueing for transient retries (configurable TTL) to prevent reactive cross-region failover.

max: agreed. I'll open a scheduler PR to add 'fw-sensitive' host label and a placement penalty. Nina please include a heuristic to auto-label hosts showing >50 flow_steer_warn in 10m.

nina: done. added runbook step in INFRA-7002: "if flow_steer_warn > 50 in 10m -> isolate-host, steer hot tenants, capture traces, open vendor ticket."

oliver: long-term note: if vendor firmware is flaky, we either: A) require stricter SR-IOV carveouts on affected hosts (higher CAPEX due to lower packing), or B) accept periodic OPEX bump from cross-region fallback and per-incident steers. Need cost modeling.

finance-bot: tagging finance owners for modeling. Also note: cross-region egress has different tax/tariff considerations across EU clusters. Will follow up.

max: monitoring now. after isolate + steer we're not seeing further cross-region traffic. eth1 tx_errors still elevated on rack-33 but no neighbor spill. Keeping this thread open until firmware repro completes.

eric: add small experiment: throttle per-VF TX on rack-33 (e.g., 300mbit) to see if driver recovers without steer. If so, we can add an automated per-host throttle policy as a cheap mitigation.

nina: quick throttle command (lab tested):
```
# on vfX
tc qdisc replace dev vf2 root htb default 1
tc class add dev vf2 parent 1: classid 1:1 htb rate 300mbit ceil 500mbit
```

tasha: thanks team. will sync with vendor on fw 2.7.1 regression and update INFRA-7002. leaving steer for 30m and will revert if stable. :eyes:
